items.title: Major GO train expansion a top priority in Mississauga, says mayor-elect
items.summary: Mississauga’s mayor-elect says bringing long-awaited new GO train service to the city is among his top priorities as he prepares to take office next month. Tens of thousands of Mississauga residents and workers and thousands more in Milton have been waiting years for expanded train service on a key GO line serving both municipalities. Two-way, all-day train service along the Milton GO route, which includes stops at a number of Mississauga stations en route to Toronto and back again, appeared to be closer to reality with word from Ontario Premier Doug Ford in early 2024 that the province was firmly behind the plan. In pledging his government’s support at the time for the enhanced GO train service in Mississauga and Milton, Ford called on the federal government “to be a full funding partner” in the initiative. Ottawa did come to the table in 2021 with a commitment to fund 50 per cent of the estimated $1-billion Milton GO improvement plan. However, the project remains in the discussion stage and a funding agreement has yet to be worked out. Following his decisive mayoral victory on Monday night, Mississauga mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo (he’ll be sworn in Nov. 16) pledged at a press conference Tuesday morning to aggressively pursue the Milton GO line expansion.

items.title: Huge Mississauga festival set to host its first-ever multi-day Halloween event
items.summary: While many festivals have struggled to regain their footing in a post-pandemic world where costs are high (and nights at home are more alluring to some), a growing festival that started in Mississauga is expanding its calendar, offering locals a multi-day, Halloween-themed event for the first time. The Mississauga Asian Night Market, which first took over Square One’s P6 parking lot in July 2024 with a multi-day celebration of food and entertainment, is hosting its inaugural sBOOky Village at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. “This year, it’s been 14 events and so many of my friends have said it’s very ambitious, but time flies,” Ruifeng (Ricky) Zhen, the organizer of the Ontario Asian Night Market Series, tells INSAUGA Canada. This year’s sBOOky Village event kicks off today (Oct. 29) and runs until Nov. 1 in Square One’s P6 parking lot. Zhen says the event, which functions as both a family-friendly Halloween and harvest festival, is the latest offering in the growing Ontario Asian Night Market series. This year alone, the festival hit multiple cities across Ontario, with multi-day food and cultural events in Toronto, Mississauga, London, Windsor, Vaughan, Oakville, Oshawa and Niagara Falls. In Windsor and Niagara Falls, Zhen says he and his team estimate that up to 30 percent of visitors came across the border. The entire year, he says, has been a whirlwind. “We had a FIFA World Cup [watch] party and the Asian Night Markets and the mid-autumn and lantern festivals and it was a different approach that provided more Asian cultural elements,” Zhen explains.

items.title: ‘Complex’ watermain fix keeps busy Mississauga intersection partially closed
items.summary: A busy intersection in Mississauga’s east end will remain partially closed a while longer as work crews repair a watermain, project leaders said. Peel Region public works officials said on Thursday the north side of the intersection at Burnhamthorpe Road East and Molly Avenue, just west of Cawthra Road, will remain closed until Nov. 4 as workers complete the repair job. In an Oct. 29 update to residents and motorists, Peel Region said “the watermain repair has been complex and required moving other infrastructure to access the underground pipe. ” The north part of the busy intersection was initially closed off the week of Oct. 19 so crews could repair the watermain. The work was expected to be completed and the intersection reopened by Oct. 26. However, work crews encountered difficulty and subsequently pushed back the completion date by just over a week. A MiWay bus stop (stop no. 1564) has been temporarily moved while workers finish the job. Public works officials remind drivers and others in the area to be careful around the work site and obey construction crews. A number of residents began asking the region earlier this week why the intersection hadn’t been completely reopened by Oct.

items.title: Dogs and cats are just $25 to adopt during Mississauga shelter event
items.summary: Looking to add a furry friend to the family? Mississauga is once again offering dog and cat adoptions for just $25 in a bid to help more shelter animals find homes before winter. The City of Mississauga’s latest Adopt-a-thon runs from Nov. 2 to 14, giving prospective pet owners a chance to save hundreds of dollars on adoption fees at Mississauga Animal Services. The reduced fee is a significant drop from the regular cost of adopting a dog or puppy, which is typically $280 plus HST, while cats and kittens can cost up to $190 plus HST. The $25 fee applies to all dogs and cats at the shelter, with HST and any applicable pet licensing fees charged separately for Mississauga residents. The promotion follows a successful August campaign when the city introduced the same $25 adoption fee after its animal shelter reached capacity for dogs. That initiative helped 53 animals find positive outcomes, according to an update from the mayor’s office. The total included 18 dogs, 22 cats, seven rabbits, five birds and one python that were adopted, placed in foster homes or transferred to nearby rescue organizations. Interest in the August campaign was strong, with the shelter receiving more than 100 calls a day and dozens of visitors. Seven dogs were adopted on the first day, while many cats found homes as soon as they became available. The campaign also helped some long-term residents leave the shelter. One dog, a 10-year-old husky and Akita mix named Kaito, had been in the shelter’s care since October 2023 before finding a new home during the promotion. Mississauga Animal Services is launching the latest event with winter approaching, a period when pet adoptions typically decline.

items.title: CBSA Dog Aggie Flags 16 Kilograms of Undeclared Goat Feet and Ghee at Pearson
items.summary: According to the Canada Border Services Agency, detector dog Aggie intercepted another large shipment of undeclared food at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga. The agency reports the seizure included 16 kilograms of goat feet, chicken, ghee and milk powder brought in by a group of travellers arriving from Pakistan. CBSA says the travellers were fined $1,350 for failing to declare the items. The agency reports this is the latest in a series of food and animal product seizures publicized at Pearson throughout 2026. According to the CBSA, Canadian law requires travellers to declare all food, plant and animal products entering the country. The agency says undeclared or improperly permitted goods can be confiscated, destroyed or ordered removed from Canada.

items.title: Morguard Marks Topping-Off of 431-Unit Rental Project Near Cawthra and Atwater
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Morguard Corporation held a topping-off ceremony this month for its Boulevard on the Green rental development at 725 Village Green Blvd. in Mississauga, with occupancy expected to begin next year. The outlet reports Brian Athey, Morguard's senior vice president of development, said the fully enclosed building marked the milestone with a ceremonial glass plaque guests were invited to sign. Insauga.com says the project, which broke ground in October 2024 near Cawthra Road and Atwater Avenue, will bring 431 new purpose-built rental units to the city across three mid-rise buildings and townhomes. According to the outlet, the property's zoning allowed for towers up to 12 storeys, but Athey said Morguard chose a lower-rise design to fit the surrounding neighbourhood of single-family homes and townhomes. The outlet reports Morguard has owned the roughly 20-year-vacant site, previously believed to have housed a postal sorting facility, for about two decades.

items.title: Ontario's Police Watchdog Finds Reasonable Grounds to Charge Halton Sergeant Over 2025 Chase
items.summary: According to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, Sgt. David Joseph of Halton Regional Police has been charged with dangerous operation of a conveyance causing bodily harm following a March 12, 2025 police pursuit in Mississauga. The SIU said in an Oct. 28 release that there were reasonable grounds to charge Joseph after the chase, which stemmed from the theft of a Kia Sedona from an Oakville home that also involved a stolen GMC Hummer. According to the SIU, the pursuit ended when the 26-year-old driver of the Hummer was seriously injured and taken to hospital. The SIU reports the investigation concluded more than a year after the incident occurred. Mississauga.com reports Joseph is the officer who led the chase through Oakville and Mississauga.

items.title: Dense Fog Prompts Near-Zero Visibility Warning Across Mississauga and Nine Other Municipalities
items.summary: According to Environment and Climate Change Canada, a yellow-level weather advisory is in effect Thursday morning for Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon, Halton Hills, Burlington, Oakville, Newmarket, Georgina and northern York Region. The agency says areas of dense fog are expected to impact the region, with visibility suddenly dropping to near zero at times. Environment Canada reports travel will likely be hazardous in some locations as a result. The agency is advising drivers to prepare for near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach their destinations. According to Environment Canada, the fog is expected to dissipate later in the morning.

items.title: Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga Introduces Guided Biofilm Therapy With Airflow Dental Cleaning in Mississauga
items.summary: Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga is now offering Guided Biofilm Therapy as an additional professional dental cleaning option for patients in Mississauga. Mississauga, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 29, 2026) - Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga has added Guided Biofilm Therapy to its dental cleaning services, expanding the options available to patients during routine professional cleanings. The addition introduces airflow dental cleaning as part of the practice's preventive care services and gives the dental team another method to consider when planning a cleaning appointment. Professional cleanings are a regular part of dental care, but the approach used during an appointment can vary depending on the patient and the condition of the teeth and gums. By adding Guided Biofilm Therapy, Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga is giving patients more choice in how routine cleaning care may be approached while keeping the overall focus on oral health maintenance. Guided Biofilm Therapy uses airflow technology as part of the cleaning process and can be incorporated when appropriate. The service is not intended to replace every traditional cleaning method. Instead, it can be considered alongside other techniques based on what the dental team observes during the appointment. The addition also gives patients an opportunity to understand how their cleaning will be approached before treatment begins. Some patients may want to know why one method is being considered over another, while others may simply prefer to understand the options available to them. Offering GBT dental cleaning in Mississauga gives the practice a clearer way to explain those choices and discuss how Guided Biofilm Therapy may fit into an individual cleaning visit. For Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga, the new service expands its preventive dental care without changing the purpose of regular cleaning appointments.
